clue.text: Dog runs on tips of toes

indicators.note: in this across clue 'on' means placed after, so the runs come at the end

parts.note: a ballet dancer up on the tips of the toes is said to be en pointe
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dog that tiptoes along at a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets R after POINTE, the ballet term for dancing on the tips of the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is a breed of gun dog that stands still with its nose aimed at game.

clue.text: Painful feelings about heading for road accidents

indicators.note: about means the feelings word goes around the road letter

parts.note: pangs are sudden sharp pains

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the word road

explanation.surface: The pain felt when heading for a series of crashes on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside PANGS. A prang is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prangs is colloquial British for crashes, especially minor collisions involving vehicles.

clue.text: Carrying a Colt and dope to gangster

parts.note: dope is slang for information
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster with a Colt revolver and drugs on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like the gun but is a young horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare that is pregnant with a young horse is said to be in foal.

clue.text: Foreign claimant is charming?

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Is a claimant from overseas charming?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' rearranges CLAIMANT IS. The question mark marks the magical sense of charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is a lucky charm, so a talismanic object works like a charm in the magical sense.

clue.text: As non-conformist, show shock when made to accept bishop

indicators.note: made to accept means the shock word takes the bishop letter inside it

parts.note: to reel is to stagger with shock
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dissenter visibly stunned when forced to take on a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made to accept' puts B inside REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is someone who refuses to go along with authority or convention.

clue.text: Liable to pay in court, as record includes arrest

indicators.note: includes means the record word holds the arrest word inside it

parts.note: a file is a record kept of something
to nab someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A legal note: whoever's record shows an arrest may face a court penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link; 'Liable to pay in court' is one definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence that is finable carries a monetary penalty, a sum a court can order paid.

clue.text: Something pour le weekend in this?

definitions.text: Something pour le weekend in this?

parts.words: Something pour le weekend in this
parts.note: the French phrase pour le weekend borrows an English word, the kind of mixture of the two languages the answer names

explanation.surface: A packing note for a trip across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'pour le weekend' uses an English loanword, a typical mixing of the two languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French peppered with English borrowings, mocked by language purists in France.

clue.text: Following 10 into trap

indicators.note: into means the numeral goes inside the trap

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: follow ten into a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is just the Roman numeral X.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what comes immediately after in a sequence; adjectives with the same meaning.

clue.text: It's painful in non-upholstered carriage

indicators.note: in says the cry of pain sits inside the bare word

parts.note: bare means without covering or upholstery
ouch is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Riding in a carriage with no padded seats hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A barouche is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with a collapsible hood.

clue.text: In leisure time, people right to cross land

indicators.note: In says the people word goes inside the pairing of leisure and time

parts.note: ease is relaxation or leisure
men are people

explanation.surface: People in their spare time exercising a right of way.
explanation.walkthrough: An easement is a legal term, which is why 'right to cross land' is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In property law an easement is a legal entitlement to use another's land, such as a right of way.

clue.text: Allowed to be executed? That's terrible

indicators.note: to be executed is to lose the head, so the word for allowed loses its first letter

parts.note: something lawful is allowed by law

explanation.surface: Is a legal execution a dreadful thing? A comment on capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be executed' means beheaded: LAWFUL loses its head, its first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very bad or dreadful; they are plain synonyms.

clue.text: High culture: dandies take selections with no pressure

parts.note: beaux are fashionable men, dandies

indicators.note: with no says the pressure letter is taken away from the selections word

parts.note: parts are portions or selections of a whole
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Dandies picking out the choicest bits of high culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes P from PARTS to give ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The beaux arts are the fine arts, such as painting and sculpture, which make up refined culture.

clue.text: Stoke thoughts of egg layer's faulty chromosome

indicators.note: faulty says the letters of the egg layer and the chromosome are wrongly arranged

parts.note: these letters, including the S of the possessive, are fodder for the anagram
Y is the male sex chromosome

explanation.surface: A hen's defective chromosome stirring genetic musings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' mixes EGGLAYERS with Y. Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard was set at Stoke Poges in Buckinghamshire, so 'Stoke' is a place, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray's famous poem records his meditations in the churchyard at Stoke Poges, a village in England.

clue.text: One month and another back in US base

indicators.note: back says the second month's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a second month, August, abbreviated Aug
M is a standard abbreviation for month

explanation.surface: Two months spent away at an American military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns only 'another' month round; the single M for 'One month' follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific island of Guam is a US territory housing major air and naval bases.

clue.text: Want allies mobilised for constituency election here

indicators.note: mobilised suggests troops moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A party wanting allies to be mobilised for a constituency election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobilised' rearranges WANT ALLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eatanswill is the fictional borough in Dickens's Pickwick Papers where a famously rowdy parliamentary election is held.

clue.text: A rat race?

parts.note: the letters A RAT form the central half of the eight letters of the long-distance footrace word, so this is a race of half length

explanation.surface: A cynical shrug at the corporate grind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags wordplay: A RAT is half the letters of MARATHON, so 'a rat race' is a race that is half of that one.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-length marathon is a road race of about thirteen miles, half the full distance.

clue.text: Fall badly, clutching broken leg with hesitation — it provides locomotion

indicators.note: clutching means the first scrambled word holds the second inside it
badly says the letters of the word fall are disordered
broken says the letters of the word leg are reassembled

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A clumsy tumble onto a broken leg, with some hemming and hawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams nest here: the first word, rearranged by 'badly', wraps around the second, rearranged by 'broken'; the hesitation sound then follows. The definition is a biology term for a cell's swimming tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagellum is the whip-like tail that some cells and bacteria use to swim.

clue.text: Almost burn top of strawberry crumble

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter of the word strawberry

parts.note: to moulder is to crumble away and decay

explanation.surface: A dessert nearly scorched in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' looks like the pudding, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly with smoke but no flame, which is not quite burning.

clue.text: Care for girl, largely one strait-laced?

definitions.meaning: care in the sense of caution and good judgement
a girl's first name, often shortened to Prue

explanation.surface: Looking after a girl who is rather prim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely one strait-laced' is a further hint: most of the name gives PRUDE, a strait-laced person.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is caution or forethought, and also a traditional English girl's name.

clue.text: It is hard to defend profit — at least most of it is wrong

parts.note: a margin is the profit made on a sale

indicators.note: is wrong says the remaining letters are put in a different order
most of it means the phrase loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A grumble that profit-making is indefensible, or mostly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of it' drops the last T of AT LEAST, leaving ATLEAS, which 'is wrong' rearranges to ALSEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In elections, a constituency held by a narrow majority is vulnerable and difficult for the sitting party to keep.

clue.text: Doll that is subjected to cruel remark

indicators.note: subjected to means placed beneath, so in this down clue the abbreviation follows the remark

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A doll at the receiving end of an unkind comment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subjected to' sets IE under BARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbie is the famous fashion doll made by Mattel.

clue.text: Back in treatment, I'd degenerated, do you see?

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A patient's complaint that treatment made things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters TIDDEG span 'treatment, I'd degenerated', and 'Back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang spelling of 'get it?', asking whether a listener has understood a joke.

clue.text: Abroad and old means ruin

parts.note: und is German for and, a foreign 'and'

explanation.surface: Overseas and elderly means financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' asks for a foreign word for 'and': German UND.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their downfall; both are verbs of destruction.

clue.text: Peace of mind, as little girl avoids serious medical condition

indicators.note: avoids means the girl's name is kept out of the condition

parts.note: heart disease is a serious illness
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: Tranquillity comes when a child escapes a grave illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoids' removes DI from HEART DISEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart's ease means tranquillity or contentment of spirit; it is also a name for the wild pansy.

clue.text: Girl's getting wines, flowers and chocolates

definitions.meaning: belonging to a girl called Rose
A British brand of boxed chocolates

explanation.surface: A girl receiving the classic romantic gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions: Rose's, rosés, the flowers, and Cadbury Roses, a well-known British tin of chocolates.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense fits the same letters: a possessive name, pink wines, blooms and a confectionery brand.

clue.text: Country church abolished out of spite

indicators.note: abolished says the church letters are removed

parts.note: malice is spite
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A nation that did away with its church out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abolished' removes CE from MALICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Put on performance of carols to be heard at Covent Garden?

definitions.text: to be heard at Covent Garden?

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: a performance of the carols reworks the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staging a carol concert at the Royal Opera House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance of' rearranges CAROLS to CARLOS. Covent Garden is the Royal Opera House in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera Don Carlos is part of the repertoire performed at London's Royal Opera House.

clue.text: I hold teaching qualification — fix?

parts.note: I'm, short for I am, as in holding the qualification: I am a graduate
BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A teacher offering a credential as the solution to a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as I'M B.ED: saying I hold the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbed (usually embed) is to fix something firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Re: woman I found in drink

indicators.note: found in says the woman and I are placed inside the drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
hen is slang for a woman, as in hen party

explanation.surface: A memo about a woman discovered in her cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re:' looks like 'regarding' but is the definition: Re is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Re is the chemical symbol of the heavy metallic element number 75.

clue.text: Water being this universal, keeping head above it?

definitions.meaning: water is called the universal liquid that dissolves things
keeping one's head above water means staying out of debt

explanation.surface: A science lesson about water, then an image of staying afloat in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the second half points back to water: keeping your head above water is staying financially afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Water dissolves more substances than any other liquid, and a business that pays its debts is in credit.
